sections.heading: Core Gameplay Loop: Planning Phase and Real-Time Defense
sections.intro: Before the outbreak begins, the game gives you a bird's-eye view of the city and reveals where the infection will start. This planning window is your opportunity to study the map, anticipate spread routes, and allocate limited resources before the situation becomes live. Choosing where to position forces and how to divide your budget during this phase shapes every decision that follows.
paragraphs: Once the infection spreads, the game shifts to real-time defense. Zombie numbers grow quickly, so the units and positions you locked in during planning are your foundation — you adapt around them rather than rebuilding from scratch. Saving civilians depends on how well your pre-outbreak plan accounts for the speed of the spread and the layout of the city.

hero.heading: Zombies Aren't Real Beginner Guide: Your First Run
hero.lead: Zombies Aren't Real gives you a planning window before each outbreak starts, showing the infection's starting location on a real-world city map. Use that time to position defenses, allocate your opening budget across ground units and air support, and establish safe zones for civilian evacuation. Your goal is to save at least 10% of the city's population—success depends on reading the map layout, prioritizing the right purchases, and adjusting your strategy as the outbreak spreads.

sections.heading: Core Gameplay Loop and How to Win
sections.intro: Each run in Zombies Aren't Real follows a clear structure: you start with a bird's-eye view of a real-world city and a marked infection origin point. Before the outbreak begins, you have a planning window to deploy military forces using your limited starting budget. Once the infection spreads, you adapt in real time by repositioning units, calling in air support, and establishing safe zones for civilian evacuation.
paragraphs: Your objective is to save at least 10% of the city's population before time runs out or the infection consumes the entire map. Success requires balancing offensive containment—slowing the horde's expansion—with defensive perimeters around evacuation zones. You lose if civilian casualties drop below the 10% threshold or if your forces are overrun and the infection reaches critical mass.

The game rewards strategic planning over reactive play. Units deployed during the planning phase cost less and start in optimal positions, while mid-outbreak purchases arrive with delay and higher resource costs. Prioritize choke points, natural barriers, and high-density civilian areas during setup, then adjust your strategy as the outbreak reveals weak points in your defenses.

sections.heading: Planning Phase: Read the City and Deploy Bar
sections.intro: Before the outbreak begins, the game gives you a bird's eye view of the city and marks where the infection will start. Use this window to scan the map for natural choke points—narrow streets, bridges, or clustered buildings—that can slow the horde and let your units focus fire. Identify evacuation routes for civilians and note any open squares or wide boulevards where zombies can flank your defenses.
paragraphs: The deployment interface shows your starting budget and available units. You'll place ground forces (infantry, barricades, or heavy weapons) and request air support strikes before the first wave spawns. Prioritize positions that cover multiple approach angles and protect the evacuation zones you identified. Since resources are limited, avoid scattering units across the entire map; concentrate them where the infection is most likely to push through first.

Once you confirm your deployment, the outbreak starts and the timer begins. You can still adjust tactics during play, but your opening setup determines whether you hold the line or lose critical ground in the first minutes. A strong planning phase lets you meet the 10% civilian survival threshold without scrambling to patch gaps mid-outbreak.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes and Next Steps
sections.intro: New players often overspend on air support in the first turns, leaving no budget for ground units when the infection reaches dense residential blocks. Another common error is placing all defenses near the spawn point instead of along evacuation routes, which lets zombies bypass your line and attack fleeing civilians. Ignoring the map's natural choke points—bridges, highways, or narrow streets—wastes the terrain advantage that could funnel infected toward concentrated fire.
paragraphs: If you lose your first few runs, try the single-player mode to experiment with unit placement without time pressure, then move to online co-op with a friend to split coverage and share budget decisions. Steam Workshop offers community maps and scenarios that isolate specific mechanics, such as defending a single district or managing a limited unit roster. Achievements also guide progression by rewarding milestone strategies, helping you identify which tactics work under different outbreak conditions.

faq.question: What should I buy first in Zombies Aren't Real?
faq.answer: Prioritize a mix of ground defenses and at least one early safe zone marker. Ground units let you establish a perimeter around the outbreak's starting point, slowing the infection while you funnel civilians to safety. Avoid spending your entire opening budget on air support—helicopters are powerful but expensive, and you'll need reserves to react when the horde breaks through your first line.

faq.question: How does the planning phase work?
faq.answer: Before the outbreak begins, the game reveals the infection's starting location on the city map and gives you a fixed preparation window. You can place units, defenses, and safe zones during this time, but nothing moves or attacks yet. Use the pause to study roads, identify natural choke points, and position your forces so they can respond the moment zombies appear.

faq.question: Where should I place my first garrison?
faq.answer: Position your first garrison at a choke point between the outbreak's origin and dense civilian neighborhoods. Look for intersections or narrow streets that force the horde into a killbox, letting a single unit cover multiple approach angles. Avoid open plazas or parks where zombies can spread in every direction—your early defenses work best when the map funnels enemies toward them.
